title: Problem transferring files via activity manager to gmail
creator: donald.pymont
content: I have transferred all my virgin media mail and folder directories across to Gmail and all seemed fine to start with and activity manager was beginning to show a transfer of folders and contents. I made the mistake of dragging all my virgin folders over to Gmail in one go. and now I have all the folders showing in Gmail but they are now all empty and activity manager shows no activity taking place. title: Severe Thunderbird performance issues with Gmail IMAP — 3–6 GB RAM, high CPU, 30-second message opening, even after clean reinstall
creator: johnny.quide
content:
Subject: Severe Thunderbird performance issues with Gmail IMAP — 3–6 GB RAM, high CPU, 30-second message opening, even after clean reinstall

Hello Thunderbird community,

I would like to report a persistent and severe performance problem when using Thunderbird with Gmail IMAP accounts. After extensive troubleshooting, Thunderbird remains practically unusable.

System configuration

- Device: Microsoft Surface Pro 7 - Processor: Intel Core i7-1065G7 - RAM: 16 GB - Operating system: Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit - Storage: 238 GB SSD - Antivirus: Bitdefender Antivirus Free - Thunderbird: Current Windows release downloaded directly from Mozilla (Date: Nov 17, 2026)

Problem

Thunderbird initially works normally with a new, empty profile.

After adding my Google Workspace account, performance was initially acceptable. However, after adding my personal Gmail account, Thunderbird became extremely slow.

Observed symptoms:

- Opening an email regularly takes approximately 30 seconds. - Reopening an email that was already displayed is just as slow. - Even opening application menus or changing settings becomes extremely sluggish. - Thunderbird occasionally displays "Not Responding" for extended periods. - RAM consumption reaches approximately 3–6 GB. - CPU usage remains around 12–14%, even when Thunderbird is offline and supposedly idle. - During these episodes, total system memory usage reaches 74–90%. - Network and disk activity can be close to zero. - On one occasion, Thunderbird appeared to start downloading IMAP headers again after the initial synchronization had already completed.

Importantly, the problem persists even when the Activity Manager shows no ongoing synchronization or indexing operations.

Troubleshooting already performed

1. Initially used the Microsoft Store version of Thunderbird. 2. Removed large local IMAP message stores (approximately 27 GB), after making backups. 3. Disabled local offline message storage. 4. Disabled global search and indexing using "mailnews.database.global.indexer.enabled = false". 5. Tested plain-text message rendering — no improvement. 6. Tested Troubleshoot Mode — performance became substantially worse, approximately five times slower. 7. Completely replaced the Microsoft Store installation with Thunderbird downloaded directly from Mozilla. 8. Created a clean profile without importing the old mailbox databases or search indexes. 9. Confirmed that the new installation worked normally before configuring the mail accounts. 10. Reconfigured Google accounts using IMAP/OAuth2, again without downloading complete offline mailboxes. 11. Allowed IMAP header synchronization to finish completely. 12. Tested offline mode — slightly faster, but still unusable. 13. Used "about:memory" → Minimize memory usage — Thunderbird became temporarily unresponsive, with no lasting improvement. 14. Confirmed that the problem is not caused simply by insufficient hardware resources.

The problem returned despite the clean installation and new profile.

Additional observations

The deterioration seems closely related to adding and processing the personal Gmail account. The Google Workspace account alone initially appeared to work normally.

My Gmail accounts contain extensive mail histories with many folders and thousands of messages. However, full offline message storage is disabled.

The application's main interface remains sluggish even when it is not actively downloading messages.

Questions for the community and developers

1. Is this a known Thunderbird performance regression affecting large Gmail IMAP accounts? 2. Could IMAP folder handling or message-list processing cause this degree of RAM consumption and sustained CPU activity? 3. Why does the problem persist after header synchronization has finished and Thunderbird is offline? 4. Could this indicate a problem with Thunderbird's internal message databases, even in a new profile? 5. Are there known fixes or specific diagnostic steps that would help identify the affected component?

I am willing to provide anonymized screenshots of Task Manager and performance diagnostics if useful.

I wanted to use Thunderbird as a long-term alternative to Microsoft Outlook, but the current performance makes that impossible.

Any suggestions or confirmation of similar experiences would be appreciated.

Thank you.
